phase3_findings.description: lib/test/run.sh:25217-25221 (and the same shape at 25182, 25184, 25191, 25193, 25199, 25204, 25235, 25263, 25267, 25365): an assertion that calls the fixture builder inline as `sbl_build "$scenario" >/dev/null 2>&1; sbl_run ...` uses `;` not `&&`, with the builder's stdout AND stderr discarded. sbl_build writes $SBL_TMP/exec.jsonl in place and never truncates it on failure, so a failed build leaves the PREVIOUS scenario's fixture on disk and the helper measures that instead. The #1897 name-binding order loop is the demonstrable fail-open: contains_name_first and contains_name_second are the same two loads in opposite order and both yield exactly 2 delivered-whole, so a builder failure on the second iteration re-measures the first's fixture, prints 2, and passes green — the ordering half of the very regression the loop exists to close goes unexercised. Swallowed causes: an absent python3, an OSError/UnicodeDecodeError reading SBL_REVIEW/SBL_IMPLEMENT/SBL_RAF, a KeyError from an unrecognised scenario key, a full or read-only $SBL_TMP. Iteration 4's fix hardened the HELPER spawn (sbl_run/sbl_says/sbl_rel_denies all gate on exit status) but left the BUILDER ungated at these call sites. Remedy: either an `sbl_count` helper mirroring sbl_says's guard, or — the cheaper partial — have sbl_build `rm -f "$SBL_TMP/exec.jsonl"` before writing, which closes the stale-fixture channel for every call site at once.

phase3_findings.description: The ambiguity arm's load-count operand is undriven — the same defect shape iteration 3's F4 fixed in the sibling never-loaded arm, in the arm F4 did not cover. scripts/skill-body-load-probe-verdict.py's verdict_for_root renders the ambiguity reason with `% (len(matches), skill_name)`. The only fixture reaching that arm is retry_after_error, which records exactly two loads BOTH of which match, so len(matches) == len(pairs) == 2 and the two operands are indistinguishable; and the only assertion reading that sentence greps 'recorded Skill loads name prflow:review', a pattern beginning AFTER the %d, so the digit is never compared at all. The agent confirmed by mutating a scratch copy: swapping the operand to len(pairs) renders a byte-identical string on this fixture. The count is load-bearing in exactly the way F4 argued: it tells a maintainer reading a red row whether two distinct loads collided or a transcript merely holds two loads of which two happen to match. Closing it costs one fixture and one assertion — a transcript with two prflow:review loads plus one unrelated prflow:implement load (three pairs, two matches), asserted to report '2 recorded Skill loads name prflow:review', which goes RED on a len(pairs) swap (it would render 3) and pins the digit.

phase3_findings.description: lib/test/run.sh:25380-25381 — the empty-selection assertion still expects grep's FAILURE arm: `sbl_run "$SBL_TMP/exec.jsonl" | grep -q 'VERDICT: delivered-whole' && echo no || echo yes` with expected value `yes`. This is the exact shape iteration 3's F1 filed and iteration 4 fixed elsewhere via sbl_rel_denies; this site was missed. A traceback from sbl_run produces no stdout, grep misses, and the assertion prints the expected `yes`. Exit-status gating is not available here (the no-roots path deliberately exits 2), so the fix is to assert a positive property instead: capture once, then require the 'AUDIT: NO-ROOTS' line present AND the 'VERDICT: delivered-whole' line absent from that same capture. phase3_findings.description: lib/test/fixtures/skill-body-load-transcript.observed.json carries a .json extension on a file whose first bytes are a '#'-commented header, so a plain json.load() of the path fails. It parses today only because parse_execution_file strips the leading '#' run first. No current lint validates tracked .json files, so nothing catches it now, but an editor, a jq sweep, or any future repo-wide JSON-validity gate reads the name and chokes. DISPUTED DETAIL, recorded rather than resolved: the final-pass reviewer reports the post-header body as JSONL, while the VC-12 verifier reports it as a whole-file JSON array that json.loads accepts after the header strip. The naming concern stands under either reading; the remedy differs (.jsonl vs a header-free .json). The fixture path is referenced from run.sh, the two coverage-map notes and the docs page, so a rename touches four sites.
